searched: RAMP global network page, About RAMP one-pager 2024, RAMP asset management page, RAMP relaunch feature (May 2025)
outcome: The World Bank does NOT publish a full named membership list. It publishes only counts, which conflict across pages: 'over 70 members' (one-pager 2024), '75th member' (Cabo Verde, April 2024), 'over 80 institutions' (relaunch feature, May 2025), 'a record 95 members' (Ecuador release, April 2026), 'more than 90' (Central Bank of Libya, Oct 2025). The asset management page states the Treasury 'manages assets for all RAMP members, totaling over $30 billion', so RAMP does run real mandates, but names no client. The global network page names only seven institutions, via staff profiles: Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago, Bank of Guatemala, Korea National Pension Service, Panama Savings Fund, National Bank of Cambodia, FAO of the United Nations, Bulgarian National Bank.
next_step: Members have to be assembled one at a time from World Bank press releases and from each central bank's own site. An email to RAMP or the paywalled Central Banking coverage ('Middle income countries form largest membership of World Bank Ramp', centralbanking.com/node/7962374) may list more.

searched: Ministerio de Hacienda sovereign funds FAQ 'Quien administra los fondos actualmente?'
outcome: FIVE RECORDS. Named current managers: BNP Paribas Asset Management, BlackRock Institutional Trust Company, Nomura Asset Management, UBS Asset Management Inc, Mellon Investments Corporation. Western Asset Management Company is named as a former manager that left in September 2024. The page states the Banco Central de Chile runs the external manager selection, manages the sovereign fixed income share itself, and supervises external managers investing in instruments eligible for the international reserves. Caveat for the map: these firms manage Chile's sovereign wealth funds rather than the central bank's own reserves, with the central bank as selector and supervisor.
next_step: Decide whether the Chile ties belong in this category or in a sovereign-fund category; if kept, the Western Asset exit could be recorded as a former tie.

target: Central Bank of Seychelles outside parties
outcome: THREE RECORDS and a near-miss. Crown Agents Investment Management (fixed income mandate from 2014, US$50m by 2022) and UBS (money market fund from 2017, US$10m) actually manage reserve assets; World Bank RAMP manages a US$100m externally managed portfolio from 2019 and also trains staff. The BIS is said to hold a small portion of Australian dollar holdings, but the report does not describe the BIS as custodian or manager, so that is not recorded.
next_step: This report is the single most detailed disclosure found. Look for equally detailed reserve management reports from other small open economies (Mauritius, Fiji, Eswatini, Lesotho, Papua New Guinea).
